places.name: Reykjavík centre
places.note: The capital and the natural base for day trips.
places.summary: Iceland's small, walkable capital and your base. Hallgrímskirkja church (lift to the tower), Harpa concert hall, the Sun Voyager sculpture and the Old Harbour are all within a 30-minute walk of each other.
facts: Free to wander; Hallgrímskirkja tower has a small fee
Geothermal pools (e.g. Sundhöllin, Vesturbæjarlaug) are cheap and very local
places.winter: Good aurora spot if you walk to the Grótta lighthouse, away from city lights.

places.name: Seljalandsfoss
places.note: Walk behind the falls (often closed when icy). Gljúfrabúi is on the same parking ticket.
places.summary: A slender ~60 m waterfall dropping over an old sea cliff right by the Ring Road. A path loops behind the curtain of water — you will get wet. Gljúfrabúi, a waterfall hidden inside a narrow canyon, is a 10-minute walk north.
facts: 5 min flat walk; loop behind falls ~10–15 min
places.winter: The path behind the falls is usually closed in icy conditions (and in thaw for rockfall). Bring microspikes. Floodlit after dark.

places.name: Skógafoss
places.note: Stairs up to a viewing platform on the right side.
places.summary: One of Iceland's biggest waterfalls: a 60 m high, 25 m wide wall of water you can walk right up to. A staircase of several hundred steps on the right leads to a viewing platform at the top, where the Fimmvörðuháls trail begins.
places.winter: The stairs can be icy. Spray freezes on the ground close to the falls.

places.name: Kvernufoss
places.note: 3 min from Skógafoss, almost always empty.
places.summary: A quieter waterfall in a mossy gorge just east of Skógar. A short walk from the parking near the Skógar Museum, and like Seljalandsfoss you can walk behind it — but with a fraction of the crowds.
places.winter: Muddy or icy path; can be slippery in the gorge.

places.name: Sólheimasandur DC-3 wreck
places.note: 4 km walk each way across the sand, or shuttle ~3400 ISK return, runs 10:00–17:00.
places.caution: Long exposed walk; shuttle runs 10:00–17:00 only.
places.summary: The fuselage of a US Navy Douglas DC-3 (C-117) that crash-landed on the black sand plain in 1973 — everyone survived. The stark wreck in an empty black desert is one of the most photographed sights in the south.
facts: ~7.5 km return on flat sand (shuttle extra when running)
places.winter: Start with 3+ hours of daylight left; easy to get disoriented in snow or fog on the open sand.

places.name: Sólheimajökull
places.note: Glacier tongue — you can drive almost to the ice. Don't go onto the glacier without a guide.
places.summary: An outlet glacier tongue of Mýrdalsjökull, the ice cap that covers the Katla volcano. A short walk from the car park brings you to a lagoon at the foot of the ice. Guided glacier walks with crampons start here.
places.winter: IMO warning (22 Jul 2026): new lagoon, thinning ice ridge on the access route and rockfall from Jökulhaus. Operators cancelled ice trips and scouted new routes; the site stays open but at your own risk. View from the moraine only; do not step onto the ice unguided. Ask operators which glacier walks actually run in November.
places.caution: IMO hazard warning 2026: changing glacier margin and rockfall. View from the moraine only.

places.name: Dyrhólaey
places.note: Rock arch and lighthouse viewpoint. Upper road is steep and can be slippery.
places.summary: A 120 m promontory with a huge natural rock arch and a lighthouse on top. From here you look along endless black beaches west and across to the Reynisdrangar sea stacks east.
places.winter: Steep gravel road to the upper lighthouse can be slippery; lower lot is easier. (Seasonal nesting closure is spring only.)

places.name: Reynisfjara
places.note: Never turn your back to the sea — sneaker waves are deadly here.
places.summary: The famous black sand beach west of Vík, with hexagonal basalt columns, a sea cave and the Reynisdrangar sea stacks offshore. Dramatic and beautiful — and genuinely dangerous.
facts: Parking 1,000 ISK (near lot) or 750 ISK (far lot), Parka
places.winter: Feb 2026 storms caused a landslide and heavy erosion: narrower beach, damaged viewing platform, cave mouth exposed. Obey the warning lights: yellow = stay out of the marked zone; red = beach closed, Hálsanefshellir cave and basalt columns closed. Autumn surf is at its worst.
places.caution: Obey the warning lights: red = beach closed.

places.name: Vík
places.note: Fuel and supermarket. Katla ice cave tours (year-round) start here.
places.summary: Iceland's southernmost village (~300 people): a red-roofed church on the hill, a black beach and views of Reynisdrangar. The last decent supermarket and fuel before the long stretch east. Katla ice cave tours start here.
facts: Good overnight base for the south coast
places.winter: The road east of Vík (Mýrdalssandur) is exposed to strong crosswinds — check road.is.

places.name: Fjaðrárgljúfur
places.caution: Lower car park only (F206 to the upper lot is an F-road). Trail may be closed in thaw.
places.summary: A serpentine canyon about 100 m deep and 2 km long, carved into soft rock with moss-covered walls. A trail follows the rim with viewing platforms looking down into the gorge.
facts: Rim trail ~3.4 km return from lower lot
places.winter: Use the LOWER car park at the end of Road 206 (gravel, OK for 2WD driven slowly). The upper lot is reached via F206, an F-road, so skip it. The Environment Agency has closed the trail during wet thaw periods to protect vegetation; Road 206 can be blocked after heavy snow. Never enter the canyon floor.

places.name: Kirkjubæjarklaustur
places.note: Small village with fuel and a shop.
places.summary: A tiny village ("Klaustur") on the Ring Road between Vík and Skaftafell. Near the village are Kirkjugólf, a natural floor of basalt columns, and the Systrafoss waterfall.
facts: Useful overnight stop for the far east

places.name: Skaftafell
places.note: Visitor centre; Svartifoss hike ~1.5 h return.
places.summary: Part of Vatnajökull National Park, below Iceland's highest peaks. The classic walk climbs to Svartifoss, a waterfall framed by black basalt columns. Another easy trail leads to the face of the Skaftafellsjökull glacier. Svartifoss is ~5.5 km return and uphill; plan 1.5–2 h and bring microspikes.
facts: Regional parking fee ~1,100 ISK; 50% off same-day second VNP area
places.winter: Trails can be icy. Glacier hikes and ice-cave tours often meet here.

places.name: Jökulsárlón
places.note: 380 km from Reykjavík. Diamond Beach is across the road. Blue ice cave tours (Nov–Mar) leave from this area.
places.summary: A lagoon full of icebergs calved from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier, often with seals swimming among them. Across the road, ice chunks wash up on the black sand of "Diamond Beach". The highlight of the south coast for most visitors.
facts: Regional parking fee ~1,000–1,100 ISK/day (Parka zone 7202); same zone as Diamond Beach; 50% off if you paid another Vatnajökull NP area the same day
places.winter: Natural blue ice caves under Vatnajökull can only be visited on guided tours, roughly November to March. Many tours meet here or in Skaftafell.

places.name: Þingvellir
places.note: Rift valley national park. Paid parking.
places.summary: A UNESCO site where Iceland's parliament, the Alþingi, met in the open air from 930 AD. It sits in a rift valley where you walk between the North American and Eurasian plates; Almannagjá gorge is the main path. Silfra fissure, famous for snorkelling, is here too.
facts: Parking 1,000 ISK (car ≤5 seats), 1,200 ISK (6–9 seats); one fee valid all day in P1–P3 and P5
places.winter: Paths can be icy; the open plain is good for aurora on clear nights.

places.name: Geysir
places.note: Strokkur erupts every few minutes.
places.summary: The geothermal field that gave all geysers their name. The Great Geysir itself is mostly dormant, but Strokkur next to it erupts every few minutes, shooting boiling water 15–30 m up. Bubbling hot pools and steaming vents surround it.
places.winter: Ground around the pools can be icy. Stay behind the ropes — the water is near boiling.

places.name: Gullfoss
places.note: Lower path can be closed when icy.
places.summary: "Golden Falls": the Hvítá river drops in two stages into a deep crevice, about 32 m in total. It is one of Iceland's most powerful waterfalls and the third stop of the Golden Circle.
facts: Free; café and toilets at the top
places.winter: The lower path to the edge of the falls is often closed because of ice. The upper viewpoint stays open.

places.name: Kirkjufell
places.note: Sleep in Grundarfjörður (hostel ~3 km away).
places.summary: The steep, arrowhead-shaped mountain (463 m) beside the village of Grundarfjörður, possibly the most photographed in Iceland. The classic view is from the small Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall across the road. It also appears in Game of Thrones.
places.winter: Do not attempt the mountain itself; it has seen fatal falls. Good aurora foreground.

places.name: Arnarstapi
places.note: Coastal path to Hellnar (~2.5 km).
places.summary: A small fishing hamlet beneath Snæfellsjökull, with dramatic basalt sea cliffs, the Gatklettur rock arch and a big stone statue of the half-troll Bárður. An easy coastal trail runs to Hellnar.
facts: Time: 45 min (1.5 h with the Hellnar walk)
Coastal path to Hellnar ~2.5 km each way
places.winter: Cliff edges have no fences — keep back in wind and ice.

places.name: Djúpalónssandur
places.note: Black pebble beach with shipwreck remains.
places.summary: A black pebble beach in Snæfellsjökull National Park, reached by a short path through lava formations. The rusted remains of the British trawler Epine, wrecked in 1948, lie across the beach. Four old lifting stones once tested fishermen's strength.
facts: NEW: Snæfellsjökull NP service fee since 13 Aug 2026, ~1,100 ISK per car, one payment valid park-wide until midnight (Parka zone 3200 or Malarrif kiosk)
places.winter: Like Reynisfjara, the surf here is dangerous — don't go near the water's edge.

places.name: Blue Lagoon
places.note: 20 min from Keflavík. Book a time slot.
places.summary: A geothermal spa with milky-blue, silica-rich water at about 37–39 °C, set in a lava field on the Reykjanes peninsula. It's pricey and touristy, but very relaxing. Only 20 minutes from the airport, so it works well before a flight.
facts: Comfort from ~11,990 ISK, Premium ~14,990 ISK (2026, varies by slot)
places.winter: Open as of late 2026, but magma under Svartsengi has passed the volume drained in the last eruption; IMO says a new intrusion/eruption on the Sundhnúkur crater row is the most likely scenario and the spa evacuates at short notice. Check bluelagoon.com and vedur.is the day before; keep a Sky Lagoon backup.
places.caution: Volcanic risk at Svartsengi: can close/evacuate at short notice. Check the day before.

places.name: Keflavík Airport
places.note: Iceland's international airport, ~45 min from Reykjavík.
places.summary: Iceland's international airport, about 45 minutes from Reykjavík. Most car-rental returns are close by, with shuttles to the terminal.
facts: Allow time to return the rental car
Fill up the tank before the return

places.name: Kerið crater
places.summary: A volcanic explosion crater about 55 m deep, with red and black walls and a lake at the bottom. A path runs round the rim and down to the water. It's an easy stop between Selfoss and the Golden Circle.
facts: Rim loop ~270 m circumference plus stairs to lake
Entrance 700 ISK per person; parking free
places.winter: The rim path can be icy; the lake may be frozen.

places.name: Faxi waterfall
places.summary: A broad, low waterfall on the Tungufljót river, with a salmon ladder beside it. It's quiet, and only a short detour off the Golden Circle road between Geysir and Reykholt.

places.name: Secret Lagoon (Flúðir)
places.summary: A natural hot-spring pool at Flúðir, kept at about 38–40 °C, with a small geyser bubbling beside it. It's smaller, cheaper and more local-feeling than the Blue Lagoon. It works well as an evening soak after the Golden Circle.
facts: Paid entry; book ahead in busy periods
places.winter: Open year-round. Soaking after dark is fine, but drive back carefully.

places.name: Laugarvatn Fontana
places.summary: Geothermal baths, hot pools and natural steam rooms on the shore of Lake Laugarvatn. Ask about the rye bread baked in the hot ground; there are demonstrations.
facts: Rebuilt: infinity pools, sauna, cold plunge, geyser steam bath; rye-bread tour extra
places.winter: Closed Oct 2025–Jun 2026 for expansion; now fully reopened.

places.name: Brúarárfoss
places.summary: A small waterfall famous for its vivid turquoise water rushing into a narrow crack. Access and parking have changed over the years: check what's current before you go.
facts: 30–45 min from new lot; 2–3 h via trail
~350 m from new lot; ~3.5 km each way from free trail lot (64.2401, -20.5241)
places.winter: New lot reached via ~3 km of gravel Brúarfossvegur off Road 37 (potholes); fine for 2WD in normal conditions. Riverside trail can be icy.

places.name: Reykjadalur hot river
places.summary: A hike up a steaming valley above Hveragerði to a warm river you can bathe in, with wooden partitions to change behind. It's one of the best free experiences near Reykjavík.
places.winter: The trail gets muddy and icy, so use microspikes. Start early: you want daylight for the walk down.
places.caution: Winter: icy trail — needs daylight both ways.

places.name: Friðheimar greenhouse
places.summary: A tomato farm in Reykholt with a restaurant inside the greenhouse. It's known for its tomato-soup lunch among the vines. It makes a good lunch stop on the Golden Circle.

places.name: Urriðafoss
places.summary: Iceland's highest-volume waterfall: the wide Þjórsá river pours over a low ledge. It's a 5-minute detour from the Ring Road east of Selfoss.

places.name: Selfoss
places.summary: The largest town in the south, on the Ölfusá river, with a newly built old-style town centre. It has supermarkets, fuel and cafés: a practical stop on the way out of Reykjavík.

places.name: Hvolsvöllur & LAVA Centre
places.summary: A small town on the Ring Road, home to the LAVA Centre. Its interactive exhibition explains Iceland's volcanoes and earthquakes, including Eyjafjallajökull and Katla. It's a good rainy-day stop.

places.name: Seljavallalaug pool
places.summary: One of Iceland's oldest swimming pools (1923), built into a mountain valley under Eyjafjallajökull and fed by a hot spring. It's unstaffed, free (donations welcome) and wonderfully remote-feeling.
facts: Walk ~20 min each way from the car park
Water is lukewarm rather than hot
places.winter: Path crosses a stream and can be icy.

places.name: Skógar Museum
places.summary: A folk and transport museum with old turf houses, a church and thousands of objects from rural Icelandic life. It's right next to Skógafoss.

places.name: Kirkjugólf
places.summary: A natural "church floor": the flat tops of basalt columns that look like laid paving stones. It's a 2-minute stop at the edge of Kirkjubæjarklaustur.

places.name: Svínafellsjökull
places.summary: A glacier tongue just past Skaftafell, with a jumble of blue ice right in front of the viewpoint. Scenes from Batman Begins and Interstellar were filmed here.
places.winter: Civil Protection advises against travel on the glacier because of a monitored rock-slope crack; guided tours are suspended indefinitely. The two unpaved access roads are unmaintained and not ploughed in winter. If accessible, stop only briefly at the viewpoint. Treat as optional; Fjallsárlón/Falljökull are safer substitutes.
places.caution: Tours suspended (rock-slope crack); access roads not ploughed in winter. Optional at best.

places.name: Fjallsárlón
places.summary: A smaller, quieter glacier lagoon 10 km before Jökulsárlón, where the glacier comes right down to the water. Many people prefer it to its famous neighbour.
facts: Parking reported free (one Jan 2026 list shows 1,000 ISK; check signage)

places.name: Diamond Beach
places.summary: Across the road from Jökulsárlón, chunks of glacier ice wash up and glitter on the black sand of Breiðamerkursandur. It's best at sunrise or sunset.
facts: Covered by the Jökulsárlón regional fee (Eystri and Vestri-Fellsfjara lots)
No facilities at beach; use Jökulsárlón
places.winter: The same sneaker-wave danger as other black beaches. Never climb on the ice blocks in the surf.

places.name: Höfn
places.summary: A harbour town an hour east of Jökulsárlón, famous for its langoustine (humar). It's the base for staying east of the glacier lagoon, and the gateway to the Eastfjords.

places.name: Borgarnes
places.summary: A small town on a peninsula an hour north of Reykjavík, on the road to Snæfellsnes. It has the Settlement Centre, a museum about the first settlers and Egil's Saga, plus fuel and food.

places.name: Hraunfossar & Barnafoss
places.summary: Hundreds of small waterfalls pour out of a lava field into the milky-blue Hvítá river. Barnafoss, a wild narrow chute, is a few steps upstream.
places.winter: Viewing platforms can be icy.

places.name: Deildartunguhver
places.summary: Europe's most powerful hot spring by flow, gushing boiling water that heats nearby towns. The Krauma spa next door uses its water.

places.name: Gerðuberg cliffs
places.summary: A long wall of near-perfect basalt columns rising from the plain. It's a quick, quiet stop on the drive to Snæfellsnes.

places.name: Ytri Tunga seal beach
places.summary: A golden-sand beach where seals often lie on the rocks offshore. They're more reliable in summer, but it's worth a look on the south coast of the peninsula.
facts: Keep a respectful distance from seals

places.name: Búðakirkja (black church)
places.summary: A small black-painted wooden church standing alone in a lava field at Búðir. It's one of the most photographed buildings in Iceland, with Snæfellsjökull behind.

places.name: Hellnar
places.summary: A tiny fishing hamlet with sea caves and bird cliffs. It's the far end of the coastal trail from Arnarstapi and has a café in a lovely spot.

places.name: Lóndrangar
places.summary: Two dramatic basalt pinnacles, the eroded remains of a crater, standing on the coast below Snæfellsjökull.
facts: Covered by the Snæfellsjökull NP fee (~1,100 ISK/day)

places.name: Saxhóll crater
places.summary: A small scoria crater with a metal staircase of a few hundred steps to the rim. From the top there's a sweeping view over lava fields and the coast in Snæfellsjökull National Park.
facts: Inside the NP, so expect the park-wide parking fee (~1,100 ISK/day)
places.winter: The stairs can be icy and the rim very windy.

places.name: Stykkishólmur
places.summary: A pretty harbour town on the north side of Snæfellsnes, with old timber houses. Climb Súgandisey island beside the harbour for views of Breiðafjörður.

places.name: Gunnuhver
places.summary: A steaming geothermal area with boiling mud pools at the tip of the Reykjanes peninsula. In folklore it's named after a ghost, Gunna, said to be trapped in the hot spring. Boardwalks lead into the steam.
places.winter: Check safetravel.is for volcanic activity on Reykjanes before you go.

places.name: Reykjanesviti & Valahnúkur
places.summary: Iceland's oldest lighthouse site, on a wild headland of sea cliffs. You can see the bird rock Eldey offshore and scramble up Valahnúkur hill.
places.winter: Road 425 is open; the SW cluster (lighthouse, Gunnuhver, Bridge Between Continents, Brimketill) has had temporary closures during eruptions.

places.name: Bridge Between Continents
places.summary: A footbridge across a sandy fissure that marks the boundary between the North American and Eurasian plates. It's touristy but fun, and right on the road.

places.name: Seltún (Krýsuvík)
places.summary: Colourful hills streaked yellow and red around hissing steam vents and mud pots, with a boardwalk loop. It's on the Krýsuvík road south of Hafnarfjörður.
facts: Parking 750 ISK (Check-it camera billing; many guides still wrongly say free)
places.winter: Boardwalks can be icy. IMO has also reported faster subsidence at Krýsuvík in 2026; no closure, but stay on paths.

places.name: Kleifarvatn
places.summary: A large, eerie lake in a rift valley with black-sand shores and lava cliffs. It's on the scenic Krýsuvík road between Reykjavík and Seltún.

places.name: Sky Lagoon
places.summary: An oceanside geothermal lagoon in Kópavogur with an infinity edge looking out to sea. Its 7-step ritual includes a cold plunge, sauna and scrub. It's 15 minutes from the centre.
facts: Passes renamed Saman (ex-Pure) and Sér (ex-Sky); Saman from ~13,990 ISK in 2026

places.name: Hallgrímskirkja
places.summary: Reykjavík's landmark church, 74.5 m tall, designed to evoke basalt columns. A lift to the tower gives the best view over the city's colourful roofs.
facts: Free to enter; tower lift is paid

places.name: Harpa concert hall
places.summary: The harbourside concert hall with a shimmering glass facade by Olafur Eliasson. You can walk in for free, and it's beautiful lit up at night.

places.name: Perlan
places.summary: A glass dome on hot-water tanks on a hill above the city, with a nature museum inside. Exhibits include a man-made ice cave, a glacier exhibition and an aurora planetarium show. There's also a 360° viewing deck.

places.name: Grótta lighthouse
places.summary: A lighthouse on a tidal islet at the tip of Seltjarnarnes, 10 minutes from the centre. There's a tiny geothermal foot bath on the shore. It's one of the best aurora spots within city limits.
facts: Islet reachable only at low tide
places.winter: Good spot for aurora on clear nights. Watch the tide if you cross to the islet.

places.name: Katla Ice Cave tour (from Vík)
places.summary: Super-jeep trip from Vík to a natural ice cave in Kötlujökull, striped with black ash from the Katla volcano. The only natural ice cave that runs year-round, so it is the safest bet in early November when Vatnajökull caves may not be open yet.
facts: Book online; crampons, helmet, headlamp included
Meet Troll Expeditions at Víkurbraut, Vík
places.winter: Runs all year; cave shape changes. Good weather back-up for a Vík night.

places.name: Vatnajökull blue ice cave tours (Jökulsárlón meeting point)
places.summary: Natural blue ice caves in Breiðamerkurjökull, reached by modified 4×4 from the Jökulsárlón car park. The classic Iceland winter image; operators include Local Guide (black trucks, main lot), Arctic Adventures (Crystal Ice Cave) and others.
places.winter: Season is roughly Nov–Mar and is set only after guides scout caves in Sep/Oct; early-November availability is thin, and in 2025 Local Guide substituted a blue-ice glacier tour when its cave was unsafe. Book refundable and confirm the week before.

places.name: Glacier Adventure base camp (Hali)
places.summary: Family-run operator whose ice-cave tours start from Hali, 10 min east of Jökulsárlón, with an ice cave + zodiac combo listed for November. Handy if you sleep at Hali/Skyrhúsið.
places.winter: November departures listed at 08:30 or 10:00; cave opening subject to conditions.

places.name: Falljökull glacier hike (Skaftafell)
places.summary: Guided crampon hike on Falljökull, a Vatnajökull outlet glacier with seracs and crevasses. The reliable glacier-walk alternative while Sólheimajökull is unstable.
facts: Icelandic Mountain Guides at Skaftafell campsite base; Melrakki at Skaftafell Terminal; Troll at Hof (free parking)
places.winter: Runs in winter; some tours add a natural blue ice cave in season.

places.name: Gljúfrabúi
places.summary: Hidden waterfall inside a narrow gorge, a short walk north of Seljalandsfoss. Same parking ticket.
facts: ~750 m flat from Seljalandsfoss; shallow stream wade to enter gorge
places.winter: Stream and rocks icy; viewing from outside is fine.

places.name: Into the Glacier – Langjökull ice tunnel
places.summary: Man-made ice tunnel high on Langjökull, reached by 8×8 glacier truck from Húsafell. Runs year-round and pairs well with Hraunfossar and Deildartunguhver.
places.winter: Winter schedule from 16 Oct; truck ride ~75 min each way. Operator says to use Roads 1, 50 and 518 to Húsafell in winter (all paved).

places.name: Vatnshellir lava cave
places.summary: 8,000-year-old lava tube entered by spiral staircases, guided by Summit Adventure Guides. A good wind- and rain-proof stop on the Snæfellsnes loop.
facts: Meet at hut above car park off Road 574
places.winter: Runs year-round with 3 tours/day in winter; NP parking fee applies.

places.name: Bjarnarhöfn Shark Museum
places.summary: Farm museum on Iceland's fermented-shark tradition, with a tasting. A warm indoor stop between Stykkishólmur and Grundarfjörður.
places.winter: Check opening hours ahead in November.
places.caution: Not fully verified — confirm it's open (and the location) before you go.

places.name: Brimketill
places.summary: Lava-rock sea pool where Atlantic swells explode against the cliffs, best on rough days. Free, short boardwalk.
places.winter: Stay on the platform: waves overtop it. Part of the Road 425 cluster that can close during eruptions.

places.name: Laugarás Lagoon
places.summary: New geothermal lagoon on the Golden Circle near Skálholt, opened October 2025. An alternative to Secret Lagoon/Fontana on the Gullfoss leg.
places.winter: Open year-round.
places.caution: Not fully verified — confirm it's open (and the location) before you go.

places.name: Hvammsvík Hot Springs
places.summary: Tidal hot pools on the Hvalfjörður shore, en route between Reykjavík and Borgarfjörður. Capped numbers make it calmer than the big lagoons.
places.winter: Open; daily numbers capped.
places.caution: Not fully verified — confirm it's open (and the location) before you go.

places.name: Skyrhúsið HI Hostel (Hali, Suðursveit)
places.summary: Renovated farmhouse hostel 10 min from Jökulsárlón and Diamond Beach, next to the Þórbergssetur restaurant and the Glacier Adventure base.
places.winter: Ideal for an early ice-cave departure.

places.name: Gerði Guesthouse (Suðursveit)
places.summary: Farm guesthouse about 13 km east of Jökulsárlón with private and shared-bath rooms and on-site dining.
places.winter: Open in November.

places.name: Vagnsstaðir HI Hostel
places.summary: Budget farm hostel 28 km east of Jökulsárlón with dorms, private rooms and cottages; remote enough for good aurora watching.
places.winter: Bring food; few dining options nearby in the evening.

places.name: Grundarfjörður HI Hostel
places.summary: Two colourful houses in Grundarfjörður, ~3 km from Kirkjufell. Central for both sides of the peninsula and for aurora shots at Kirkjufellsfoss.
places.winter: Best Snæfellsnes base in November.

places.name: The Freezer Hostel & Culture Centre (Hellissandur)
places.summary: Arty hostel and theatre in a former fish factory at the western tip, close to the national park, Vatnshellir and Djúpalónssandur.
places.winter: Confirm November opening when booking.

places.name: Hvammstangi
places.summary: A small harbour village just off the Ring Road, with the Icelandic Seal Centre. It's a sensible first night if you're heading north with a short daylight window.
places.winter: The Ring Road north crosses Holtavörðuheiði and Öxnadalsheiði, mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or briefly closed in November. Check umferdin.is before you set off.

places.name: Blönduós
places.summary: A Ring Road town at the mouth of the Blanda river, roughly halfway between Reykjavík and Akureyri. It's the practical overnight stop for breaking up the drive north.
places.winter: The Ring Road north crosses Holtavörðuheiði and Öxnadalsheiði, mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or briefly closed in November. Check umferdin.is before you set off.

places.name: Hvítserkur
places.summary: A 15 m basalt sea stack shaped like a drinking dragon or troll, standing in the surf off the Vatnsnes peninsula. A steep path leads from the viewpoint down to the beach.
facts: ~30 km of gravel road (711) off the Ring Road
places.winter: Road 711 is gravel and can be rough or icy; the path down to the beach is steep. Allow plenty of daylight.

places.name: Kolugljúfur canyon
places.summary: A narrow gorge on the Víðidalsá river with the Kolufossar waterfalls, a short detour from the Ring Road in Víðidalur.
places.winter: Gravel access; viewpoints can be icy.
places.caution: Location approximate — check the pin before you rely on it.

places.name: Glaumbær turf farm
places.summary: One of Iceland's best-preserved turf farmhouses, now part of the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum. It gives a real sense of how people lived in the 18th and 19th centuries.
places.winter: Usually only open in summer; in winter it's typically by arrangement. Check before you go.

places.name: Akureyri
places.summary: The capital of the North and Iceland's second city, at the head of the long Eyjafjörður fjord. It has a lively small centre, a landmark church, a botanical garden and a ski area above town.
places.winter: The Ring Road north crosses Holtavörðuheiði and Öxnadalsheiði, mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or briefly closed in November. Check umferdin.is before you set off.

places.name: Forest Lagoon (Skógarböðin)
places.summary: A newer geothermal lagoon set in the forest just across the fjord from Akureyri, with views back over the town. It's a good place to end the day once the light has gone.
places.caution: Location approximate.

places.name: Goðafoss
places.summary: The "waterfall of the gods": a broad horseshoe of falls on the Skjálfandafljót river. In the sagas, the lawspeaker threw his pagan idols in here when Iceland converted to Christianity in 1000 AD. It's right by the Ring Road between Akureyri and Mývatn.
facts: Café and shop by the car park
places.winter: Paths to the edge can be icy, and spray freezes in winter.

places.name: Reykjahlíð (Mývatn)
places.summary: The main village on Lake Mývatn, with a supermarket, fuel and guesthouses. It's the natural base for the volcanic sights around the lake.
places.winter: In early November many Mývatn businesses run reduced hours. Book accommodation ahead.

places.name: Skútustaðagígar pseudocraters
places.summary: A cluster of "pseudocraters" on the south shore of Lake Mývatn. They formed when lava flowed over wetland and the water flashed into steam. An easy walking loop leads around them.
places.winter: Paths can be icy.

places.name: Dimmuborgir
places.summary: A maze of towering, twisted lava pillars and arches east of Lake Mývatn. In folklore it's home to the Yule Lads.
facts: Marked loop trails of different lengths
places.winter: Trails can be snowy; stick to the marked paths.

places.name: Hverfjall crater
places.summary: A huge, near-perfect tephra ring about 1 km across, rising above the plain east of Mývatn. A steep path leads to the rim, and you can walk all the way round.
facts: Steep gravel path to the rim
places.winter: The path is often icy and the rim very windy in winter. Only climb in good conditions.

places.name: Grjótagjá
places.summary: A small lava cave with a crystal-clear geothermal pool inside, in the rift near Mývatn. It became famous from Game of Thrones.
places.winter: The entrance is a scramble over rocks, which can be icy.

places.name: Mývatn Nature Baths
places.summary: The North's answer to the Blue Lagoon: a milky-blue geothermal lagoon on a hillside above Lake Mývatn. It's smaller, calmer and cheaper, and great for aurora on clear nights.
places.winter: Open year-round, with an evening soak possible after dark.

places.name: Hverir (Námafjall)
places.summary: A steaming, sulphur-yellow geothermal field below Námafjall, with boiling mud pots and roaring fumaroles. It's right beside the Ring Road east of Mývatn.
facts: Stay on the marked paths: the ground is hot and fragile
places.winter: Icy boardwalks; the smell of sulphur is strong.

places.name: Krafla & Víti crater
places.summary: Víti is an explosion crater with a turquoise lake inside, at the Krafla volcanic system north of Mývatn, beside the geothermal power station.
facts: Short walk around part of the rim
places.winter: The road up to Krafla (863) isn't always cleared in winter. Check before you go.

places.name: Dettifoss
places.summary: Often called Europe's most powerful waterfall: the grey glacial river Jökulsá á Fjöllum thunders 44 m into a canyon. Selfoss is a short walk upstream.
facts: ~1 km walk each way from the west-side car park
places.winter: Use the paved west-side road (862). The east-side road (864) is gravel and usually closed in winter. Snow can close 862 too, so check before you drive.
places.caution: Check road 862 the day before; winter service can be limited.

places.name: Ásbyrgi
places.summary: A horseshoe-shaped canyon with 100 m cliffs, part of Vatnajökull National Park. According to legend, it's the hoofprint of Odin's eight-legged horse Sleipnir. Short forest trails lead to a pond at the end of the canyon.
places.winter: Reach it via road 85 from Húsavík; the gravel road from Dettifoss (862 north) is closed in winter.

places.name: Húsavík
places.summary: A pretty harbour town known as Iceland's whale-watching capital, with a wooden church and the Whale Museum. It's a possible base north of Mývatn.
facts: Whale watching runs on a reduced winter schedule
places.winter: Winter boat trips depend on weather; book flexible tickets.

places.name: GeoSea baths
places.summary: Geothermal sea baths on the cliffs above Húsavík, looking out over Skjálfandi bay towards the mountains.
places.winter: Open year-round; check winter opening hours.
places.caution: Location approximate.

places.name: Stokksnes & Vestrahorn
places.summary: A black-sand spit with dunes beneath Vestrahorn, a jagged, almost 900 m mountain wall that's one of Iceland's most dramatic photo spots. The land is private: you pay at the Viking Café to drive out onto the point.
facts: Small entry fee at the Viking Café
Short gravel road off the Ring Road east of Höfn
places.winter: Windy and exposed; the dunes and beach are best in low winter light.

places.name: Hvalnes lighthouse & beach
places.summary: An orange lighthouse on a gravel spit between a lagoon and the open sea, below the striped Eystrahorn mountain. It's a quick stop right by the Ring Road.

places.name: Djúpivogur
places.summary: A quiet harbour village at the southern end of the Eastfjords. Look for Eggin í Gleðivík, 34 granite eggs on the harbour wall, each representing a local bird.
facts: Eggs sculpture: 5 min from the centre
places.winter: Mountain road 939 (Öxi) to Egilsstaðir is gravel and closed in winter. Take the coastal Ring Road via the fjords.

places.name: Breiðdalsvík
places.summary: A tiny fishing village where the Ring Road reaches the Eastfjords coast. There's a hotel and a café-brewery, handy as a stop between Höfn and Egilsstaðir.

places.name: Petra's Stone Collection
places.summary: A lifetime's collection of rocks, crystals and minerals gathered from the eastern mountains, filling a house and garden in Stöðvarfjörður. It's quirky and charming.
places.winter: Opening hours are reduced outside summer; check ahead.

places.name: Fáskrúðsfjörður
places.summary: The "French village" of the Eastfjords, where French fishermen were based in the 19th century. Street signs are in French and Icelandic, and the old French hospital is now a museum and hotel.
facts: French museum in the old hospital

places.name: Egilsstaðir
places.summary: The East's main town and service centre, on the Lagarfljót lake, with an airport and supermarkets. It's the natural base for Hengifoss, Seyðisfjörður and Stuðlagil.
places.winter: Between Mývatn and Egilsstaðir the Ring Road crosses the high Möðrudalsöræfi plateau, one of the first stretches to close in snow. Check umferdin.is; the coastal Ring Road via the fjords is lower but long.

places.name: Vök Baths
places.summary: Geothermal floating pools in Lake Urriðavatn, just outside Egilsstaðir, with a cold-water plunge straight into the lake. It's a relaxing end to a short winter day.
places.winter: Open year-round.
places.caution: Location approximate.

places.name: Seyðisfjörður
places.summary: An arty fjord village of colourful wooden houses at the end of a deep fjord. The famous rainbow-painted street leads to the little blue church. The ferry to Denmark leaves from here.
places.winter: It's reached over the 600 m Fjarðarheiði pass, which is often snowy or closed in winter. Check umferdin.is and don't count on getting back the same evening in bad weather.
places.caution: Mountain pass (Fjarðarheiði) on the only road in.

places.name: Hengifoss
places.summary: One of Iceland's tallest waterfalls, about 128 m, falling past striking red clay layers between the basalt. On the way up you pass Litlanesfoss, which is framed by basalt columns.
places.winter: The path is often icy and muddy; bring microspikes and start early.

places.name: Hallormsstaðaskógur forest
places.summary: Iceland's largest forest, a rare sight in a mostly treeless country. Easy trails lead through birch and larch along Lake Lagarfljót, home of the legendary Lagarfljót wyrm.

places.name: Stuðlagil canyon
places.summary: A canyon lined with spectacular hexagonal basalt columns, revealed when a hydro dam upstream lowered the river. The best view is from the east side, after a walk of a few kilometres from the car park.
facts: East-side walk ~5 km return from the car park
places.winter: The gravel access roads can be snowed in or icy; the walk down into the canyon is steep. In November, treat it as weather permitting.
places.caution: Winter access on gravel roads is uncertain — check before driving.

places.name: Möðrudalur (Fjallakaffi)
places.summary: Iceland's highest farm, a short detour off the Ring Road on the bleak Möðrudalsöræfi plateau, with a turf-roofed café serving soup and coffee. It's a welcome break on the long drive between Mývatn and Egilsstaðir.
places.winter: Between Mývatn and Egilsstaðir the Ring Road crosses the high Möðrudalsöræfi plateau, one of the first stretches to close in snow. Check umferdin.is; the coastal Ring Road via the fjords is lower but long.

places.name: Búðardalur
places.summary: A small village at the head of Hvammsfjörður, on the road from Borgarfjörður towards the Westfjords. It's a practical stop for fuel and food before the long drive north-west.
places.winter: Westfjords roads cross several mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or closed in November, and some roads get little or no winter service. Check umferdin.is every morning and keep a spare day.

places.name: Hólmavík & the Witchcraft Museum
places.summary: The main village of the Strandir coast, home to the quirky Museum of Icelandic Sorcery & Witchcraft. Its exhibits on 17th-century spells and witch trials are both grim and fascinating. It's the gateway to Ísafjörður on the winter route around Ísafjarðardjúp.
places.winter: Westfjords roads cross several mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or closed in November, and some roads get little or no winter service. Check umferdin.is every morning and keep a spare day.

places.name: Drangsnes hot tubs
places.summary: Three free geothermal hot tubs right on the seafront of a tiny fishing village, looking out at the island of Grímsey. You can change in the building across the road.
places.winter: Short detour from Hólmavík on road 645; check the road in winter.

places.name: Ísafjörður
places.summary: The capital of the Westfjords, a lively little town on a gravel spit inside a steep fjord, with old timber houses and the Westfjords Heritage Museum. It's the base for the northern Westfjords.
facts: ~450 km / 6 h+ from Reykjavík via Hólmavík
places.winter: Westfjords roads cross several mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or closed in November, and some roads get little or no winter service. Check umferdin.is every morning and keep a spare day.

places.name: Bolungarvík & Ósvör
places.summary: A fishing town just north of Ísafjörður, reached through a tunnel. At its edge, Ósvör is a restored 19th-century fishing station with turf huts and drying racks.
places.winter: The Bolafjall viewpoint road above town is closed in winter.

places.name: Suðureyri
places.summary: A tiny fishing village at the mouth of Súgandafjörður, through a long tunnel from Ísafjörður. It has a geothermal swimming pool and a quiet harbour.

places.name: Flateyri
places.summary: A small village on a spit in Önundarfjörður, protected by large avalanche barriers built after a deadly avalanche in 1995. There's an old general store museum and a lovely fjord view.

places.name: Dynjandi
places.summary: The "Jewel of the Westfjords": a broad, 100 m high waterfall spreading like a bridal veil down a rock staircase, with smaller falls below. A path climbs past them to its foot.
facts: ~15 min walk up to the main fall
places.winter: It's on road 60 over Dynjandisheiði, a high pass that's often closed or very icy in winter. Check umferdin.is; the Dýrafjarðargöng tunnel links it to Ísafjörður.
places.caution: Road 60 over Dynjandisheiði: frequent winter closures.

places.name: Hrafnseyri
places.summary: The birthplace of Jón Sigurðsson, leader of Iceland's 19th-century independence movement, with a small museum, a turf house and a church in a quiet fjord.
places.winter: Westfjords roads cross several mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or closed in November, and some roads get little or no winter service. Check umferdin.is every morning and keep a spare day.

places.name: Reykjafjarðarlaug pool
places.summary: A simple outdoor pool with a natural hot pot beside it, in the empty Arnarfjörður landscape near Bíldudalur. It's free and usually deserted.
places.winter: Westfjords roads cross several mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or closed in November, and some roads get little or no winter service. Check umferdin.is every morning and keep a spare day.
places.caution: Location approximate; road access in winter uncertain.

places.name: Bíldudalur & Sea Monster Museum
places.summary: A fishing village in Arnarfjörður, a fjord with a long history of sea-monster sightings. The Icelandic Sea Monster Museum collects the eyewitness stories.
places.winter: Westfjords roads cross several mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or closed in November, and some roads get little or no winter service. Check umferdin.is every morning and keep a spare day.

places.name: Patreksfjörður
places.summary: The largest village in the southern Westfjords, with shops, fuel and a pool. It's the base for Látrabjarg and Rauðasandur.
places.winter: Westfjords roads cross several mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or closed in November, and some roads get little or no winter service. Check umferdin.is every morning and keep a spare day.

places.name: Látrabjarg
places.summary: Europe's westernmost point: a sheer bird cliff up to 440 m high and 14 km long. In summer it's crowded with puffins and razorbills, which have left by November. In winter it's wild and empty.
facts: ~1.5 h each way from Patreksfjörður on gravel road 612
places.winter: No birds in November, and road 612 is gravel with no winter service, so it may be impassable. Stay well back from the cliff edge.
places.caution: Remote gravel road, no winter service.

places.name: Rauðasandur
places.summary: A 10 km sweep of red-gold sand below steep cliffs, one of Iceland's most unusual beaches.
facts: Steep, winding gravel road 614 down to the beach
places.winter: Road 614 is steep gravel with hairpins and no winter service, so only attempt it in dry conditions.
places.caution: Steep gravel road, unsafe when icy.

places.name: Hellulaug hot pot
places.summary: A small natural hot pool right on the shore of Vatnsfjörður near Flókalundur, with views straight out over the water.
places.winter: Westfjords roads cross several mountain passes that are often snowy, icy or closed in November, and some roads get little or no winter service. Check umferdin.is every morning and keep a spare day.

links.note: Alerts; leave a travel plan. Emergency: 112.

checklist: Highland F-roads are all closed in November, regardless of vehicle.
Heading north: the Ring Road crosses Holtavörðuheiði and Öxnadalsheiði, high passes that ice up early. Check umferdin.is and don't plan a tight schedule over them.

Heading east of Mývatn: the Ring Road over Möðrudalsöræfi is high and exposed, and the passes to Seyðisfjörður (Fjarðarheiði) and Öxi (939) are often closed in winter. Use the coastal Ring Road through the fjords.

Westfjords in winter: allow at least 3–4 days, check umferdin.is every morning, and keep a spare day — passes like Dynjandisheiði and Steingrímsfjarðarheiði close in snow, and some side roads get no winter service.
Winter tyres are required from 1 November.
Wind damage is usually not covered by standard rental insurance — check the policy.
Open car doors with both hands — gusts rip doors off hinges.
Most sites charge parking by number-plate camera (Parka / Check-it apps or kiosks), typically 750–1,100 ISK; pay within the deadline shown to avoid a fine.
Check road.is and vedur.is the evening before and the morning of each drive.
Fill up when you can — fuel stations are sparse east of Vík.
Plan to be off the road before dark where possible; keep headlights on at all times (required).
